title: Sharp Expected Length of Honest Confidence Intervals for Binary-Outcome Experiments
banked_reason: Mathematical and decision panels PASS with no findings, four citations verified-attested; cold novelty gate caps delivered paper at subfield, score ceiling 7.2 < field 7.4, salvageable=false. Independent MAIN validity confirms below-field stop. Incomplete Lean scaffold retained; F3-F5 not completed, no Lean certification.
gap_reasons: The delivered frontier is restricted to binary fixed schedules, unconditional 95% coverage, and connected intervals; it establishes no broader inference framework.

The prospective sample-size expansion does not establish usable savings at operational trial sizes: the reported finite checks verify coverage and dual validity, rather than near-optimality of the canonical Airy intervals.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Supervisor-authorized source repair made the interval and lower certificates uniform over admissible certified choices and supplied a canonical finite deterministic evaluator with stopping, tie, and termination rules. Mathematical and decision panels passed without findings, but the cold novelty gate capped the delivered package at subfield (7.2 < field 7.4), with no in-scope salvage. The retained Lean scaffold is incomplete; F3-F5 did not complete and this archive supplies no Lean certification.
tldr: For fixed binary potential outcomes, the theorem evaluates the smallest worst-schedule expected length of a 95\% honest connected interval over all outcome-independent designs and randomized original-record interval kernels: \(\ell_n=2z n^{-1/2}-zC_A n^{-5/6}+o(n^{-5/6})\), through all integers with no surviving parity branch. An explicit counting-measure lower certificate and finite exactly calibrated connected interval algorithm match at this order. The proofs are uniform over admissible certified endpoint and certificate enclosures; a specified deterministic pair supplies a total finite witness without deciding equality of computable reals.
gap: Unrestricted squared-risk optimality and exact interval computation do not determine unrestricted honest expected length. The first changed proof step is coverage-constrained optimization of whole interval actions. The sharp correction requires an integrated discrete testing-cost expansion, not weak normal convergence.
fill: Match an all-procedure lower certificate with exact connected inversion at a remainder smaller than the derived correction. The resulting \(N(d)\) is a prospective precision benchmark for binary risk-difference experiments.
